Nivel de vechime: Nivel mediu de experiență
Tip de angajare: Full-time
Sectoare de activitate: Protecție împotriva incendiilor, Securitate și investigații și Siguranță publică
Join the team that protects our world - and be part of building something exciting 😊
 As part of APi Group, Chubb Fire & Security helps protect millions of people, buildings and critical assets around the world. From hospitals and schools to airports, commercial buildings and essential infrastructure, our work helps safeguard the environments people rely on every day.
 Now, we are building our Europe Capability Centre in Bucharest and looking for talented professionals who want to be part of something from the very beginning.
 This is more than just a new job or a new team. It is an opportunity to help create, influence, upgrade, digitalize, optimize processes while also contributing to the culture as ways of working that will define who we are. Your ideas, experience, and perspective will play an important role in how we collaborate, learn and support each other.
 We want to create an environment where collaboration, ownership, continuous learning and improvement and wellbeing are at the heart of how we work. We believe that growth can happen in all directions - through new responsibilities, new skills, cross-functional opportunities, international exposure and the chance to contribute beyond your immediate role. No matter your position, your ideas, experience and ambitions can help shape both your own career and the future of the organization.
 If what we are building resonates with your ambitions, values and aspirations for the future, we would love to hear from you 🌟
 APi International ECC is seeking for a Cyber Security Engineer – M&A Integration to assesses the cyber risk of companies we acquire and brings their IT environments up to our security standards, safely and on a deal-driven timeline.
 You will join deal teams early and stay through Day 1 readiness, integration and handover to steady-state operations. Acquired companies often arrive with unmanaged assets, legacy systems, inconsistent identity controls and unknown exposure. Our own requirements are strict, so you will need to balance risk reduction, business continuity and the speed the deal demands.
 Responsibilities 
 The work follows the life of a deal, from pre-signing diligence to handover into business as usual.
 1. Due diligence and risk assessment
Run security due diligence on target companies: architecture, network and cloud posture, identity and access, endpoint and email security, vulnerability and patch management, and third-party dependencies.
Review the target's security history, including past incidents, breach disclosures, pen test and audit findings, and open remediation items.
Assess compliance exposure against relevant regulations and frameworks (e.g. SOC 2, ISO 27001, PCI DSS, HIPAA, GDPR, NIS2, DORA, depending on the target).
Evaluate the security of the target’s products, source code and software supply chain where relevant to deal value.
Quantify findings in business terms: severity, likelihood, remediation cost and effort, and effect on valuation, deal terms or integration timeline.
 2. Deal terms and Day 1 readiness
Define Day 1 minimum security requirements: what must be in place before the acquired entity connects to our network, identity systems or data.
Design interim controls for high-risk environments, such as network segmentation, restricted access, enhanced monitoring and compensating controls.
Coordinate threat monitoring around announcement and close, when the target and our own staff become more attractive phishing and fraud targets.
 3. Integration and remediation
Build and run a security integration plan for each acquisition, with prioritized remediation roadmaps and agreed risk acceptance where timelines require it.
Integrate acquired identity and access into our enterprise model: directory and SSO consolidation, MFA enforcement, privileged access management and passwordless adoption.
Roll out our standard security stack to acquired endpoints, servers and cloud workloads, including EDR, logging to the SIEM, vulnerability scanning, and email and web security.
Migrate or retire legacy systems, shadow IT and end-of-life infrastructure in line with our policies.
Align cloud environments to our landing zone standards, including guardrails, configuration baselines and key management.
Work with Infrastructure, IT and application owners to remove blockers, and escalate where integration risk exceeds appetite.
 4. Governance, handover and improvement
Track exceptions, risk acceptances and remediation to closure, and report integration status and residual risk to leadership.
Hand over completed integrations to security operations, GRC and IAM teams with documented architecture and runbooks.
Maintain and improve the M&A security playbook: diligence checklists, scoring models, Day 1 baselines and integration patterns.
Capture lessons learned after each deal and feed them into standards and tooling.
Partner on divestitures and carve-outs when needed, including secure separation of data, access and shared services.
 Required Qualifications 
5+ years in information security engineering, architecture or consulting, with hands-on experience across identity, network, endpoint and cloud security.
Experience assessing the security posture of an unfamiliar environment quickly, and turning findings into prioritized, actionable recommendations.
Working knowledge of enterprise identity platforms (Active Directory, Entra ID or equivalent), SSO, MFA and privileged access.
Hands-on experience with at least one major cloud platform (AWS, Azure or GCP) and its native security controls.
Familiarity with security frameworks and standards such as NIST CSF, NIST 800-53, ISO 27001, CIS Controls and SOC 2.
Experience with core security tooling: EDR, SIEM, vulnerability management and email security.
Ability to explain technical risk to non-technical stakeholders, including executives, legal counsel and deal teams, in business terms.
Comfort handling highly confidential information and working under non-disclosure and deal-timeline pressure.
 Preferred Qualifications 
Direct experience supporting M&A activity, whether on a corporate security team, at a consulting or advisory firm, or on a deal-focused integration team.
Experience with multiple integrations or carve-outs, including environments in different industries, sizes and maturity levels.
Background in third-party and vendor risk management, or in software supply chain and application security.
Experience with Zero Trust architecture, network segmentation and secure connectivity (SD-WAN, ZTNA) for onboarding acquired entities.
Experience with passwordless authentication (Windows Hello for Business, passkeys, FIDO2) at enterprise scale.
Familiarity with regional and sector regulation relevant to cross-border deals, such as GDPR, UK GDPR, NIS2, DORA, HIPAA or PCI DSS.
Scripting or automation skills (PowerShell, Python, Terraform) for assessment and remediation at scale.
Experience with cyber risk quantification (e.g. FAIR) and translating findings into financial impact.
 Certifications (one or more valued): CISSP, CISM, CISA, CCSP, GIAC (GSEC, GCIH, GPEN, GCLD), OSCP, or cloud security certifications such as AWS Security Specialty, Azure Security Engineer (AZ-500) or Google Professional Cloud Security Engineer.
 Skills and attributes 
 Risk judgment: Separates deal-breakers from fixable issues, and sizes risk by business impact rather than raw vulnerability counts.
 Rapid assessment: Builds an accurate picture of an unfamiliar environment from limited access, interviews and documents.
 Architecture: Designs secure integration patterns and interim controls that work with legacy and heterogeneous systems.
 Stakeholder influence: Gains buy-in from deal teams, IT leaders and acquired-company staff without direct authority.
 Communication: Writes and presents findings clearly for executives, legal counsel and engineers, each at their own level.
 Discretion: Treats pre-announcement deal information with strict confidentiality.
 Adaptability: Handles shifting timelines, incomplete information and parallel deals without losing rigor.
 Pragmatism: Holds firm on strict requirements while offering workable paths, compensating controls and documented exceptions.
 Additional Information 
 APi Group is a global, market-leading business services company providing statutorily mandated and contracted services across its Safety Services and Specialty Services segments, including fire and life safety, electronic security, elevator and escalator, and infrastructure services. With more than 600 locations in over 20 countries, APi is built on a century of expertise, a people-first culture, and its purpose of Building Great Leaders®. In 2026, Api Group is celebrating its 100-year anniversary and its debut as a Fortune 500 company. More information is available at apigroupinc.com
